items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: a letter from Bob Weinstock to Thelonious Monk releasing him of his contractual obligations to Prestige

ctx.x: Fine. Okay. The world has gone on to other forms of waylaying people. I mean I’m not old enough to have been around when the press gangs were kidnapping sailors and putting them on ships in the harbor, but this is almost it. But no the point is so what I’m saying is it’s a combination of a certain amount of osmosis. Pop music was in the air to a very large extent and it was very close to being or actually was jazz at this point, and then also physical circumstances made it possible for me to have direct listening…

in those days that I did not realize the impossibility of what I wisely set out to do, but on the spot it was a big, sprawling Greenwich Village studio living room, Monk and I went off into a corner disregarding all the other people there and I interviewed him for an article that appeared in the magazine. A number of years later when I had a fledgling record company and had heard the accurate rumor that Monk, who at that time was with Prestige, was very unhappy with where he was, they were not happy with him, he…
Well it’s almost like the fact that you were so new to it was to your advantage.

items.title: Orrin Keepnews — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was indicating, with great scorn, Mr. Weinstock. Now, that’s a story, since both participants with me in that conversation are no longer with us, which can be used.

ctx.x: Into Riverside, or Prestige? He came to your office?

He came in. What happened was, Weinstock had come…our office, I don’t really remember why…we were on West 48th street, and Prestige was on West 50th street. Miles was curious. Where was Weinstock going in the name of them? Really curious when he saw where he was going, so he walked in moments afterwards. So, we got involved in a conversation in which I said…I got it now. We had some recent albums on the wall, including a couple of Randy Weston. I had, no, I look around and saw that Miles was looking at these…
compulsions? These were the people that I was living with! They were doing what they felt they had to do! I’m the same story.
